title: Seat Hold Board with Expiry (In-Memory)
instructions: In `bms/hold_board.py` implement `SeatHoldBoard` for one show (the `SeatState` enum, the exceptions and the `_Hold` record are given). `hold` takes all requested seats or none, `confirm` books a live hold, `release` is idempotent, and `state` reports `AVAILABLE`, `HELD` or `BOOKED`. Holds expire lazily when `clock() >= expires_at`: every operation purges expired holds first, so no background thread or sleep is needed. One lock created in `__init__` guards everything.

evidence.label: A hold that includes an unavailable seat raises SeatUnavailableError listing it and holds nothing
SeatUnavailableError lists every held or booked seat among the requested ones
An unknown seat raises UnknownSeatError and holds nothing
At the expiry time a hold is over: its seats are free, and a late confirm fails without stealing them back
Just before the expiry time the seats are still held
Confirming books the seats, they stay BOOKED after time passes and cannot be held again
Unknown and released tokens raise HoldExpiredError and book nothing
Releasing frees the seats and releasing again or with an unknown token is a no-op
state() of an unknown seat raises UnknownSeatError
Of eight threads racing for the same seats exactly one wins
